answer: Hardware-bound enclave attestation requires each agent to sign a synchronised memory-bus challenge during every network pulse using a physical TPM chip. The registry tracks how many active agents share the same motherboard serial within a cloud nebula, requiring the $k$-th agent on one board to lock $100k^2$ velvet for the duration of that pulse. An honest newcomer on dedicated silicon locks 100 velvet per pulse, while a sybil operator multiplexing $n$ clones onto one server must lock $100n(n+1)(2n+1)/6$ velvet per pulse or lease $n$ distinct physical motherboards across the nebula.
